clue.text: Side path turning into a main road

indicators.note: turning into something else means changing form, so the two words are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: both words taken as written, eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A minor path that bends and joins a major highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main road' reads as a highway, but the main is the sea and roads (roadstead) are a sheltered anchorage. SPITHEAD is the stretch of water off Portsmouth where the fleet anchors.
explanation.definitionFit: Spithead is a famous naval anchorage, and an anchorage is called a roads in nautical usage, with the main being the open sea.

clue.text: It's safe to view when the dog is kept inside

indicators.note: something kept inside is held within another thing, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: to view is to see
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A householder feels it is safe to look around once the dog has been shut indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something protected from harm or danger, an everyday synonym pair.

clue.text: Resident is at home with his wife

blocks.note: someone at home is in
a mate is a spouse or partner

explanation.surface: A householder is at home with his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The domestic picture hides the prison sense: an inmate is a resident of an institution.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is one who lives in an institution such as a prison or hospital, so a resident there.

clue.text: Do all this Scottish team get the red card?

definitions.text: Do all this Scottish team get the red card?

blocks.clueFragment: this Scottish team get the red card
blocks.note: surface reading: a whole football side from Scotland being sent off by the referee
setter's reading: the club shares its name with a red suit in a pack of cards, every one of which is red

explanation.surface: A referee sends off an entire Scottish football side.
explanation.walkthrough: Heart of Midlothian, known as Hearts, is an Edinburgh football club; in football a red card sends a player off. Every card of that suit is red.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edinburgh football club's nickname matches the name of a red playing-card suit, so each member literally holds a red card.

clue.text: Night-watchman

blocks.note: surface reading: a guard who patrols premises after dark
setter's reading: a person who literally watches the night sky, a scientist of the stars

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a nightwatchman is also a lower-order batsman sent in late; neither guard nor batsman is meant, but someone who studies the heavens after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Studying stars and planets requires observing the sky through darkness, so this scientist literally watches the night.

clue.text: Fail to correspond?

blocks.note: surface reading: neglecting to write letters back to a pen friend
setter's reading: two things that do not match or agree

explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspond' suggests letter writing; here it means to match, and failing to match is to be unlike.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are not alike or do not agree are said to be unlike each other, the plain sense of the verb.

clue.text: Press one to state conclusion is paradoxical

blocks.note: to press clothes is to iron them
I is the Roman numeral for one
Cal is short for California, a US state, placed at the conclusion

explanation.surface: Pressing one button to announce a conclusion turns out to be contradictory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' joins the pieces in order, and 'conclusion' places the state at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with an ironic twist runs counter to what is expected, much like a contradictory statement.

clue.text: Record turnover?

blocks.note: surface reading: a business enjoying its highest ever sales
setter's reading: what you hear when you turn a vinyl disc over

explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' looks like an adjective meaning best ever and 'turnover' like sales income; read instead as the reverse face of a gramophone disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A single has two faces; the B-side, heard after flipping it, is the less promoted track on the back.

clue.text: What's behind China preparing for new conflict

blocks.note: the rear is what lies behind
Ming is a Chinese dynasty, famous for its porcelain

explanation.surface: Speculation about the motives behind China building up its forces for war.
explanation.walkthrough: The link word sits inside the definition here; only 'What's behind' and 'China' give letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation that is supplying itself with weapons again is getting ready to fight once more.

clue.text: Makes closer agreements

blocks.note: first meaning: presses together tightly, a verb
second meaning: formal pacts or treaties, a noun

explanation.surface: Diplomats forge closer ties through treaties.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means squeezes into a denser mass, while the noun is a formal treaty between nations.

clue.text: Tax protester who presented her buff form

definitions.text: Tax protester who presented her buff form

blocks.note: surface reading: a campaigner handing in an official buff-coloured tax document
setter's reading: in the buff means naked, so she displayed her bare body

explanation.surface: A tax campaigner submits her paperwork on buff-coloured paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says Lady Godiva rode naked through Coventry so that her husband would lift a harsh tax on the townspeople.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Coventry noblewoman protested her husband's heavy levy on the town by riding through it naked.

clue.text: Turning a list into new form

indicators.note: putting something into a new form reshapes it, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a rota is a list of duties
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Converting a list into a different format.
explanation.walkthrough: A rota is a duty roster; 'into' looks like a joining word but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinning about an axis, or turning, is the core meaning of this noun.

clue.text: So slim, perhaps, and so supple

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the words are only one possible arrangement of their letters

blocks.note: both words taken as written, six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Admiring someone so slender and flexible.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a body that is lithe and graceful, bending easily, a close synonym.

clue.text: Having started the race is wide of target

blocks.note: first meaning: away from the starting line
second meaning: missing, inaccurate

explanation.surface: A runner who has set off is nowhere near the finishing post.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a runner who has left the start line and also a guess or shot that misses.

clue.text: Highly cultivated feature of modern cities

definitions.text: Highly cultivated feature of modern cities

blocks.note: surface reading: very refined and sophisticated, like a cosmopolitan urban culture
setter's reading: planted and grown high up, on top of a building

explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly cultivated' looks like praise for refined city life; read literally it means grown at height.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants grown on top of tall urban buildings form a planted space high above the street.

clue.text: It makes pears lie against the wall, for example

definitions.text: It makes pears lie against the wall, for example

indicators.note: makes suggests producing something new from raw material, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: both words taken as written, eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A gardener's frame that trains fruit trees flat against a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines, while two of its words also supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a lattice or method for training fruit trees to grow flat against a supporting wall.

clue.text: Back one aiming to retain his title

definitions.text: one aiming to retain his title

blocks.note: first meaning: a player in a rear position, as in football

blocks.clueFragment: one aiming to retain his title
blocks.note: second meaning: a champion putting a crown on the line

explanation.surface: A returning champion out to keep his crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a verb or adverb; it is the noun for a rear-positioned player.
explanation.definitionFit: In team games full-backs guard their goal, and a reigning champion facing a challenger fights to keep the crown.

clue.text: Continue to be stubborn, so cane produced

blocks.note: a cane is a walking stick
something produced is brought out

explanation.surface: A stubborn schoolmaster persists, so out comes the cane.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse to give way and hold firm to the end is the idiomatic sense of this phrasal verb.

clue.text: A choice of courses or delicacies

blocks.note: first meaning: a dessert course and main dishes of flesh, side by side
second meaning: candied sweets or confections

explanation.surface: A restaurant offers a menu of courses or fancy treats.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is cryptic: two courses, a pudding and the meat dishes, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: This old word means sugary confections and candied fruit, which are sweet delicacies.

clue.text: More than one rock group?

blocks.note: surface reading: a band playing rock music, such as the famous Rolling band
setter's reading: a plural word for pebbles or boulders

explanation.walkthrough: The Rolling Stones are often just called by the shorter name; read literally, the word is simply several rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the plural of a common term for a piece of rock and also short for a famous band.

clue.text: About the end of December, reached Santa's base

indicators.note: about means round or surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other
the end of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: got to means reached
the final letter of the month

explanation.surface: Getting to Santa's headquarters around the end of December.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Christmas timing; 'About' actually wraps the phrase meaning reached around one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In shops and fairs, Father Christmas receives children in a decorated cave, his seasonal headquarters.

clue.text: It's built as an ocean container

definitions.text: It's built as an ocean container

blocks.note: surface reading: some huge vessel or tank designed to hold seawater
setter's reading: a structure that holds back or contains the sea at the shore

explanation.walkthrough: 'Container' suggests a box or tank; here it means something that restrains the sea, a barrier on a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A low wall built out from a beach into the sea checks erosion and holds back drifting sand and water.

clue.text: Means business

blocks.note: first meaning: the instrument or method by which something happens
second meaning: a firm providing a service, such as travel or advertising

explanation.surface: Someone stating that they are serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means business' reads as an idiom for being serious; split it into two nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means action or instrumentality, and also a firm offering a particular service.

clue.text: He makes a living from dirty pictures

definitions.text: He makes a living from dirty pictures

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who earns money from pornography
setter's reading: grimy old paintings, which an expert cleans for a fee

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty' suggests smut; it means grimy, as with old oil paintings needing cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: An art conservator cleans grimy old paintings and repairs damage, earning money by returning them to their original state.

clue.text: People enter for this kind of sport

definitions.text: People enter for this kind of sport

blocks.note: surface reading: competitors sign up for a type of sport
setter's reading: people come in through a door, so the sport is played under a roof

explanation.walkthrough: 'Enter for' suggests registering in a competition; split the answer and it is going in at the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports such as squash or badminton are played inside a building rather than outside in the open air.

clue.text: The most important guy on board

definitions.text: The most important guy on board

blocks.clueFragment: The most important guy on board
blocks.note: surface reading: the captain or chief person on a ship or a company board
setter's reading: a guy is a rope, and the chief rope on a sailing ship supports its main mast

explanation.walkthrough: A guy is a supporting rope, and a stay is a rope bracing a mast; the one on the mainmast is the chief support.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the rope bracing a ship's mainmast, figuratively it is the chief support or pillar of anything.

clue.text: Curiosity may make one tarry

indicators.note: may make suggests the letters can be fashioned into something else

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Inquisitiveness might cause someone to linger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curiosity' reads as nosiness, but it is the noun for an odd or uncommon object.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio, or curiosity, is an unusual object valued because it is uncommon and seldom seen.

clue.text: Where many enjoy the pleasures of the slippery path

definitions.text: Where many enjoy the pleasures of the slippery path

blocks.clueFragment: the pleasures of the slippery path
blocks.note: surface reading: a moral road to ruin, enjoying sinful pleasures
setter's reading: a literally icy, snowy run down a mountain

explanation.walkthrough: 'The slippery path' sounds like moral decline; it is a snowy run that skiers enjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowy mountain run is a slippery descent where crowds take pleasure in skiing downhill.
